### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via IObjectQLEngine (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItemCached (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via IObjectQLEngine (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2efa81586180b3ac7b7dcae7dcb3ab45e5367454` — the merge of head `7f3638c5bcacab92670113fbc367a58c1e211eab` into base `776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2efa81586180b3ac7b7dcae7dcb3ab45e5367454 && git checkout 2efa81586180b3ac7b7dcae7dcb3ab45e5367454
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610 7f3638c5bcacab92670113fbc367a58c1e211eab && git checkout -B drift-repro 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610 && git merge --no-ff 7f3638c5bcacab92670113fbc367a58c1e211eab

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8bfac916b83df754c3e712655a85048ae8d980f6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts + packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-cascade.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (on `main`, the `object` arm), .changeset/28001-cascade-delete-objects-beside-item.md, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the gate the changeset is judged by), content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, content/docs/references/api/app-bundle.mdx, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json

Face: published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`, non-test). Nothing narrows, so no narrowing face is added. Card #28001, ruling record 6545218189 (B), seat claim 6545641008, dev report 6546528911. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no human login is named under ③.

### ① Derived judgments

Each acceptance-set and public-surface change the diff makes, judged on the committed tree against `origin/main` (merge base `4bc077d2`):

1. `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.cascadeDeleteObjects: string[]` optional, no default (`protocol.zod.ts`). CORRECT. Widening only: an absent key still parses, `[]` survives as `[]`, a non-string entry is refused at `['cascadeDeleteObjects', 0]`; absence is never defaulted to `[]`, so "no engine answered" and "nothing cascades" stay distinct, as the describe text promises. Pinned in `meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts`, type-level and runtime.
2. `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema.cascadeDeleteObjects: string[]` optional (`protocol.zod.ts`). CORRECT. Same shape; its describe text says "never part of `etag`" and that the method never answers `notModified` for a read that carries it, which is what `getMetaItemCached` does on this head (the `ifNoneMatch` stand-down now also requires `cascadeDeleteObjects === undefined`).
3. `IObjectQLEngine.getCascadeDeleteObjects?(objectName: string): string[] | undefined` (`contracts/objectql-engine.ts`). CORRECT as an optional member on the `getFlowRegistration?` / `getDisabledActions?` shape: an engine that lacks it still satisfies the contract, and the only caller (`resolveCascadeDeleteObjects`) type-checks `typeof read !== 'function'` before calling. The docblock's "three members are optional by ruling" sentence is updated to match.
4. `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/GetMetaItemCachedResponse:cascadeDeleteObjects` and `api/GetMetaItemResponse:cascadeDeleteObjects`. CORRECT as the mechanical companion of 1 and 2 (the shard already lists `disabledActions` the same way). But see ②: this file moving is what the changeset gate reads as a metadata-protocol change, and it decides the level.
5. Public `ObjectQL.getCascadeDeleteObjects(object)` (`engine.ts`). CORRECT. `undefined` when `_registry.getObject(object)` is falsy, otherwise `collectCascadeDeleteObjects` over `resolveObjectName(object)` and `getAllObjects()`. The delete walk's `cascadeRelationBehavior` matches the target "by raw or resolved name", so the resolved form here and the form `delete()` passes reach the same relations.
6. The served key on `GET /meta/object/:name`, both doors, and on the app bundle's object entries. CORRECT and in scope of the ruling ("through object metadata"). On the non-cached door it is produced in `getMetaItem` under the same condition as `disabledActions` (`!execution && decorated` present), so it is absent on the execution face and on a draft read, and absent on every type other than `object` (`resolveCascadeDeleteObjects` returns `undefined` before touching the service table). The list read (`GET /meta/object`) deliberately carries none; declared in the PR body and the changeset, pinned by a test.
7. No change to the acceptance set of any authorable document: `item` is served as stored, the key sits beside it, and no schema under `packages/spec/src/data/**` moves. The object save body is parsed by the `.strict()` `ObjectSchema`, so a `cascadeDeleteObjects` an author writes inside an object definition is refused as an unrecognised key, and the envelope key has no write address at all (the PUT body is the item). This is the same posture `disabledActions` has; no new refusal is needed and none is added.

### ② Semver level

Declared: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset. CORRECT: a new optional key on two response schemas, a new optional contract member and a new public engine method; nothing that ran before is refused.

Declared: `Metadata-protocol: none`, with `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest` in one changeset. WRONG on this repo's rules, and the head is already red on it. This answers the dev's open question (option B, not A):

- `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` is the authority on detail for AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, and its level axis reads a declared `none` as refused whenever the diff moves a `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard: "a changed authorable-surface shard is a key added or removed — a metadata-protocol change the ratchet can see" (verdict `none-baseline-moved`, exit 1). This PR moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`.
- The head's `Check Changeset` check run concludes `failure` with exactly that annotation: "Moved: packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json … Declare `Metadata-protocol: added`, `narrowed` (with the `(narrowing)` arm) or `semantic` and grade the package at least `minor`."
- The #27842 precedent (landed as #27964, `3e0fd7a8f`) is the same shape and took the gate's reading: `.changeset/27842-disabled-actions-beside-item.md` graded `@objectstack/spec` `minor` under `Metadata-protocol: added`, and a second changeset graded `metadata-protocol`, `rest`, `objectql`, `runtime` `patch`. The gate accepts that split as `discharged` (a kind declared, one moved package at `minor`, the others at `patch`, #16361).
- The dev's reading of step 3 ("the change to what a metadata author can write") is the prose; where the gate enforces the rule mechanically, the script's header is the authority on detail (AGENTS.md preamble), and the gate's baseline rule is deliberate: the ratchet cannot tell a served key from an authorable one, so a key added to any shard-listed schema is `added`.

Ruling the seat can adopt: `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`; `objectql`, `metadata-protocol`, `rest` stay `patch` (either as one changeset with mixed levels or split as #27842 did; both read `discharged`). The lockstep `fixed` group versions every package at the highest bump anyway, so the choice carries no release cost.

MUST-FIX (② declaration): change the `Metadata-protocol:` line to `added` in the PR body and in `.changeset/28001-cascade-delete-objects-beside-item.md`, and grade `'@objectstack/spec': minor` there. A kind other than `none` also owes the PR body the `Skills-docs:` line the pm-dispatch declaration row names; `Skills-docs: none — a served-only key, nothing an author writes or a skill teaches` is the honest value here. Re-read `Check Changeset` green on the new head before ACCEPT. This is a declaration and changeset edit only; no source moves, so the resulting head is a delta re-review, not a new full round.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag `open_questions[0]` (changeset level, `status: for_contract_review`): answered above, option B. Must-fix recorded.
- Order ruling "one rule": HOLDS. `cascadeRelationsInto` is the former inline `cascadingInto` body lifted out byte-for-byte in logic (same loop, same `cascadeRelationBehavior(target, child, fieldName, fdef) === 'cascade'` test, same result shape); `collectCascadeDeleteSet` now calls it through the same per-target memo it had, so the delete's behaviour is unchanged. The grep of `protocol.zod.ts`, `protocol.ts` and `meta-item-read-routes.ts` on the head finds `cascade` / `deleteBehavior` / `master_detail` only in prose and describe text. No second copy.
- Order ruling "object-level, never `inspectCascadeDelete` or row counts at a user door": HOLDS. `getCascadeDeleteObjects` reads `getAllObjects()` and no row; `inspectCascadeDelete` is untouched and is not reachable from any door on this diff.
- Order ruling "no authorable key" and "no `ui/**`": HOLDS. No `ui/**` path in the diff; no authorable schema moves (① item 7).
- Dev deviation "object names, not fields": ACCEPTED as within the order's "pick one shape" latitude. The reason is real on `main`: `createMetaItemReadGate`'s `object` arm serves the whole document to any caller with a resolved context and prunes only `listViews`, while a field of another object can be removed whole by that object's ADR-0106 mask; a field name in the list could therefore disclose a masked field, an object name discloses nothing an object read does not.
- Dev deviation "two single-file vitest runs outside os-verify-lock": process note, no contract effect.
- Out-of-scope note "the list read carries none": agreed, and the acceptance set says so. The ui card the seat files at landing is the consumer.
- Dev's "NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`": CI runs it; nothing in this diff touches a build entry.

### ④ Design judgment

`protocol.zod.ts` against ruling B and its first consumer: the key is what the ruling asked for, a server-served list the delete confirmation names objects from, with no engine rule copied client-side. Its position beside `item` is the right one: it is derived from other objects' definitions, so it is no part of this object's document and can never be saved back. The prose on both schemas is precise about the three states (absent, `[]`, names) and matches the code on every count I read: production in `getMetaItem`, the cached door's 304 stand-down, the REST door's ETag fold.

`contracts/objectql-engine.ts` against the engine: the member is optional on the established shape and its contract text (transitive, each object once, breadth-first first-reach order, self only on a cycle back, `restrict`/`set_null` not named, `undefined` for an unknown object) is what `collectCascadeDeleteObjects` does. Cycles: `expanded` is seeded with the root and each child is expanded once, so a self-cascading tree names itself once and terminates (pinned, `cd_folder`), and a two-object cycle terminates by the same set. Transitivity: it is the object-level closure of `collectCascadeDeleteSet`, which expands only objects whose rows were actually reached; the served list is therefore the superset "what a delete MAY remove", which is the right semantics for a confirmation. The agreement test (a real `delete()` of `cd_parent` empties exactly the named objects) pins the two walks to each other.

Visibility (order: "follow the rule the metadata answer already applies"): the served list is caller-independent, and the object read on `main` withholds no object by permission, so the list cannot name an object the caller could not read by name. Not a leak and not a must-fix. One reading for the ui half: the list is the process registry's closure, the same `getAllObjects()` the delete itself walks, so any scoping question is the delete's own, not one this key introduces.

ETag and cache: the REST door folds `cascadeDeleteObjectsFingerprint` as the outermost fold after `disabledActionsFingerprint`, through `cachedDisabledActionsFingerprint` (`''` for absent, a hash of the JSON list otherwise); `foldVisibilityFingerprintIntoEtag(etag, '')` is the identity, so an object no engine answered for keeps its validator byte-for-byte (pinned). The fold order of the five existing dimensions is unchanged; the restructured nesting is the same sequence with one more fold. The list is the same for every caller, so folding it into a shared validator discloses nothing per-caller. The protocol-level `getMetaItemCached` stands its own 304 down when the key is present, exactly as for `disabledActions`, and the REST door's own comparison decides. Correct.

`content/docs/references/**` (AGENTS.md: never hand-edited): the PR's diff there is only the seven new table rows (five in `app-bundle.mdx`, two in `protocol.mdx`), zero other lines; each row's text equals, character for character, the corresponding `.describe()` string on the head (the item describe for the five bundle rows and one protocol row, the cached describe for the other), and the row counts match `disabledActions`' footprint on `main` minus the list-read row this PR does not add. That is the generator's output for this spec change, not a hand edit; `check:generated` in CI is the mechanical confirmation.

`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: one row, the new metadata-protocol test's `findOne` double, beside the identical row for `protocol.object-disabled-actions.test.ts`. Expected mechanical companion.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-qxo0yv`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

One must-fix, in ②: the `Metadata-protocol: none` + `patch` declaration is refused by the changeset gate because `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` moves; declare `added`, grade `@objectstack/spec` `minor` (others stay `patch`, the #27842 shape), add the `Skills-docs:` line, and the record on the new head is a delta review.
